observations: Three photos show the same industrial sewing machine from slightly different angles.
The machine is cream-colored with a gray metal base and has visible wear, including scuffs and dirt.
The brand 'TYPICAL brother' is visible on the front panel in all photos.
A model plate is visible below the caution label, reading 'BROTHER' and '000-015'.
The machine has a large pulley on the right side, suggesting it is belt-driven or motorized.
No power cord, foot pedal, or accessories are visible in any photo.
The machine is placed on a tiled floor in front of a dark, textured door.
The seller claims it is 'complete set working perfectly and ready to use'.

claims.claim: This comes in complete set working perfectly and ready to use
claims.evidence: No photos show the power cord, foot pedal, or any accessories. No operation is shown. The machine appears worn, but no signs of damage or malfunction are visible.

risks.risk: The machine may not be complete (missing power cord, foot pedal, or accessories)
risks.proof: Photo showing the full set including power cord, foot pedal, and any other accessories.

risks.risk: The machine may not be working despite the seller's claim
risks.proof: Video clip showing the machine in operation, including the needle moving and the motor running.

risks.risk: The machine may have internal damage or wear not visible in photos
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the needle, bobbin area, and motor housing, or video of the machine running under load.

proof_requests: Video of the machine in operation, including the needle moving and motor running.
Photo showing the complete set: power cord, foot pedal, and any other accessories.
Close-up photo of the needle, bobbin, and motor housing to check for damage or wear.
response.reason: The machine is identifiable as a Brother 000-015 industrial sewing machine, but the seller's claim of being 'complete and working perfectly' cannot be verified from the photos alone. Missing accessories and lack of operational proof create significant risks that must be resolved before pricing.
